questions.question_text: During a road test, the vehicle struggles to accelerate uphill. A scan tool shows no fault codes related to engine performance. What is the most likely cause of this issue?
questions.option_a: Fuel delivery system malfunction (fuel pump or injectors)
questions.option_b: Air intake restriction due to a clogged air filter
questions.option_c: Exhaust restriction from a partially blocked catalytic converter
questions.option_d: Transmission slipping, causing reduced engine load
questions.explanation: Fuel delivery issues can significantly affect the vehicle's performance. A malfunctioning fuel pump or injectors could lead to insufficient fuel flow during acceleration, especially under load.
questions.topic: engine power loss under load, fuel delivery, air intake restriction, exhaust restriction, transmission slip, sensor diagnostics

questions.question_text: Upon visual inspection of the engine compartment, you notice a loose vacuum hose connected to the throttle body. What is the most likely immediate effect on the vehicle's performance?
questions.option_a: Increased fuel consumption due to richer air-fuel mixture
questions.option_b: Reduced power output due to air intake restriction
questions.option_c: Decreased engine temperature leading to poor combustion
questions.option_d: Exhaust backpressure causing reduced engine efficiency
questions.explanation: A loose vacuum hose can cause an air intake restriction, leading to a leaner air-fuel mixture and reduced power output.
questions.topic: engine power loss under load, fuel delivery, air intake restriction, exhaust restriction, transmission slip, sensor diagnostics

questions.question_text: During a diagnostic test, you observe that the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor is reading higher than normal values. What could be causing this issue?
questions.option_b: Air intake restriction due to a clogged air filter
questions.option_c: Exhaust restriction from a partially blocked catalytic converter
questions.option_d: Transmission slipping, causing reduced engine load
questions.explanation: A clogged air filter can restrict the airflow into the engine, leading to higher than normal MAP sensor readings.
questions.topic: engine power loss under load, fuel delivery, air intake restriction, exhaust restriction, transmission slip, sensor diagnostics

questions.question_text: You suspect a potential issue with the throttle position sensor (TPS). Which of the following symptoms would you expect to observe during a road test?
questions.option_a: Vehicle accelerates smoothly without any issues
questions.option_b: Vehicle struggles to accelerate, especially at low RPMs
questions.option_c: Engine idles roughly and stalls frequently
questions.option_d: Exhaust emissions are significantly higher than normal
questions.explanation: A faulty TPS can cause the engine to misinterpret throttle position signals, leading to improper fuel delivery and reduced acceleration.
questions.topic: engine power loss under load, fuel delivery, air intake restriction, exhaust restriction, transmission slip, sensor diagnostics

questions.question_text: During a pressure test of the fuel system, you notice that the fuel pressure is lower than expected. What could be causing this issue?
questions.option_b: Air intake restriction due to a clogged air filter
questions.option_c: Exhaust restriction from a partially blocked catalytic converter
questions.option_d: Transmission slipping, causing reduced engine load
questions.explanation: A malfunctioning fuel pump or regulator can result in lower than normal fuel pressure, affecting the vehicle's performance during acceleration.
